text:
inc-bot: ⚠️ SEV2: cross-region health-check oscillation detected (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). Increased tail latency and elevated 5xx rate on generation/chat routes. Pager: https://pd.example/INC17456
Sam W: ACK. I'm joining. Observed start ~04:07 UTC. Paging oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: acknowledged, joining.
Priya K: health probe logs show quick flips: us-west hc=500 @04:07:12, eu hc=500 @04:07:40, us-east hc=502 @04:08:05, then back. Windows ~20-30s.
deploy-bot: FYI I had a control-plane deploy at 04:06:58 that pushed health-agent config to a subset of hosts.
Jorge L: routing system reacts to hc state immediately; because we have zero dampening, traffic is bouncing and causing fallback to slower model variant (v1-quant) intermittently. That variant spikes token latencies.
Ethan M: Impact: some customer sessions see 2-3x latency on long-context calls and a handful of requests hit 503. Support dashboard shows 12 customers with alerts; top two account alerts are high.
Mira R: CS prepping communications. Suggest short status: "Investigating intermittent routing instability causing elevated latency. Mitigation in progress."
Sam W: mitigation proposal: 1) temporarily disable automated cross-region fallback; 2) pin affected routes to v2-onnx; 3) restart health-agent in regions that flapped. Any objections?
Priya K: I support. We'll lose automatic failover but avoid chasing flaps.
Ethan M: I'll prepare the per-route pin.
oncall-sre: executing: `infractl routing policy update --hold-fallback --incident INC17456`
oncall-sre: completed. Policy state=HOLD.
Jorge L: observed traffic stop rebalancing within 45s; majority stayed in us-west (primary for affected routes). Tail latency trending down.
Priya K: restarting health-agent in eu and us-east now (staggered; keep primary region alive). Restart logs: restart issued to eu cluster at 04:09:30, us-east at 04:10:15.
deploy-bot: re: control-plane deploy: it incremented probe concurrency limit to 200 for faster scan; looks like the probe client rate limiter was not tuned and under burst it returned errors. Opening issue.
Ethan M: pinned routes to stable model: `platform api routes patch --route chat/* --model v2-onnx --incident INC17456`
Mira R: posted incident snippet to status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC17456 and flagged top 5 customers for outreach.
Priya K: probe latency p99 before restart peaked at 2.1s, post-restart back to ~50ms. No hc=500 seen for 10 minutes.
Jorge L: logs indicate probe bursts coincide with control-plane telemetry flushes from 04:06:55-04:07:10. Hypothesis: burst + probe client rate limiter -> false negatives.
Sam W: action items: (A) implement dampening/exponential backoff for fallback policy (B) make probe client resilient: additive jitter + token-bucket limit + retry with backoff (C) add canary and throttling to control-plane deploys that touch health agents.
oncall-sre: monitoring for 20m stable window.
Ethan M: leave model pin in place for 45m then evaluate.
Mira R: CS templates ready for proactive outreach if needed.
Sam W: assigning postmortem to Jorge L. Please include timeline, deploy correlation, and proposed config changes. Expected draft in 3 business days.
Jorge L: will include PR link and test plan.
inc-bot: oncall handoff note: next rotation will be @Priya K for primary if pager escalates.
Priya K: taking handoff. If we see new flaps I'll escalate to infra-network.
Sam W: summary: mitigation successful by holding fallback + model pin + agent restarts. Root cause likely probe client rate-limiter + control-plane deploy burst. We will follow-up with config changes and deploy safety checks.
Mira R: will prepare customer-facing summary after PM review.
oncall-sre: incident remains open until 1h stable. Monitoring shows success rate returned to baseline and latency normalized.
Sam W: thank you all. Will update when SEV status changes.
